Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with acute pain and swelling of the left wrist. Imaging
confirmed a distal radius fracture, and examination findings were consistent with that diagnosis. The mechanism of injury, a
lateral force transmitted through an outstretched hand, is in keeping with the type of fracture seen. Initial management consisted
of immobilization and pain control, followed by a structured rehabilitation program. Over the course of 22 visits the patient
progressed steadily, with decreasing pain, improving range of motion, and increasing grip strength. Visit frequency was reduced
as recovery advanced, in line with the expected course for this injury. No prior injury or treatment to the same area is recorded in
the patient's history. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service, with no duplicated entries. The patient
has been discharged to independent home exercise with follow-up as needed.
</page>
